newsitem.title: USA: NYNEX says merger process on track in NY.
newsitem.headline: NYNEX says merger process on track in NY.

text.p: NYNEX Corp said on Thursday that a breakdown of talks with special interest groups in New York State will not affect either the timing or chances of approval of its merger with Bell Atlantic Corp.

The talks were arranged by staff on the New York Public Utilities Commission, aiming -- somewhat optimistically -- for a jointly written proposal to be submitted to the full Commission hearings on the merger.
"It was a predictable conclusion," said NYNEX spokesman Bob Varettoni, noting the differing stands that consumer groups and the phone company have taken on the merger.

The New York Citizens Utility Board said talks ended Thursday morning, and said it would now put its own case formally before the commissioners in a brief. NYNEX will do the same, and the Commission will rule in February.
Five of the seven NYNEX states have either approved or left unopposed the proposed stock swap to combine NYNEX and Bell Atlantic.

Consumers groups say the merger removes a potential competitor -- Bell Atlantic -- which might otherwise have muscled into NYNEX territory, and are looking for bigger cuts in phone rates than the combined group has proposed.
They are also critical of NYNEX's patchy service record, and concerned about universal service in the state.
The merger partners maintain that the merger gives them the resources to offer phone services more economically and reliably than was possible before.
